reasoning.text: The 'spec' is a 3D floorplan/geometry description (part shapes, positions, materials, and a physical assembly narrative), not an RTL specification — it carries essentially none of the numeric parameters, bit-widths, arithmetic, or control logic needed to rebuild the actual NTT accelerator. Both engineers (each at confidence 37) had to invent the modulus, widths, Barrett constants, the central conflict-free mapping equation, the radix-4 arithmetic, the FSM, timing, and handshakes, and they diverged on nearly all of them. It conveys what the machine looks like, not what it does, so the underlying system is not reproducible from it.
gaps: [param] Modulus q value (spec says only '14-bit'; both guessed 12289)
[width] Coefficient / BRAM word width and transform length N
[operation] Conflict-free address-to-bank mapping equation (the core algorithm)
[control] Crossbar permutation pattern per NTT stage
[param] Barrett parameters: constant mu, shift amount k, number of conditional corrections
[width] DSP multiplier product width and intermediate reduction widths
[operation] Radix-4 butterfly arithmetic: which twiddle powers (W^0,W^k,W^2k,W^3k) feed which add/sub, where the 4th-root multiply lives
[param] Twiddle ROM depth, contents, and address ordering
[param] INTT N^-1 constant value and exact application point
[control] Schedule/FSM state sequence, loop bounds, and how radix-2 vs radix-4 reconfigures the datapath
[timing] Pipeline depth per stage, total latency, and initiation interval
[port] Streaming handshake/back-pressure protocol (valid/ready/stall) and port widths on every bus/FIFO
